Threat: Phishing leads to account takeover
Vulnerability: Staff not trained to spot phishing; MFA only partly enforced
Existing controls: Spam filtering in Microsoft 365; MFA on email for some staff
Planned control: Enforce MFA for all accounts, passkeys for administrators, annual phishing awareness training

Threat: Administrator account compromised
Vulnerability: Not all admin accounts use MFA or passkeys; admin rights are broad
Planned control: Require passkeys or hardware security keys for all admins; apply role-based access and least privilege

Threat: Customer data exposed
Vulnerability: Network access and firewall settings not reviewed regularly
Planned control: Restrict access to private endpoints only; quarterly review of database configuration

Threat: Malware through unpatched software
Vulnerability: No documented patch process or deadline
Planned control: Define 14-day patch deadline for critical updates and monitor compliance through device management

Threat: Lost or stolen device exposes data
Vulnerability: Disk encryption exists but is not enforced or verified
Planned control: Enforce and verify disk encryption on every laptop; enable remote wipe

Threat: Company email data leaks from unmanaged phones
Vulnerability: No device management, screen lock or app protection rules
Planned control: Require app protection policy for work email (Microsoft Intune) or restrict email to managed apps

Threat: Leavers keep access after departure
Vulnerability: No documented joiner, mover and leaver process
Existing controls: IT administrator removes access when told, with no set deadline
Planned control: Documented leaver checklist agreed with management; access removed on the last working day

Threat: Data cannot be restored after an incident
Vulnerability: Backups are never tested
Planned control: Quarterly restore test; document recovery time and recovery point targets

Threat: Supplier outage or breach affects customers
Vulnerability: No supplier security review or register
Planned control: Create supplier register; review security documents and data processing agreements for the three key suppliers

Threat: Single point of failure
Vulnerability: One part-time person holds all administration knowledge
Planned control: Document admin procedures; give a second trusted person emergency (break-glass) access

Threat: Secrets such as keys or passwords leaked in code
Vulnerability: No secret scanning or push protection
Planned control: Enable secret scanning and push protection; rotate any secret found

Threat: Developer account compromised
Vulnerability: MFA not enforced for every organisation member
Planned control: Enforce MFA and single sign-on through Entra ID; require branch protection and code review

Threat: Leaver copies or keeps source code access
Vulnerability: GitHub is not part of the leaver checklist
Planned control: Add GitHub, Azure and support tool to the leaver checklist (see R07)

Threat: Attack goes unnoticed
Vulnerability: No central logging, alerting or defined log retention
Planned control: Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud and central logging with alerts; define log retention

Threat: Real customer data exposed through testing
Vulnerability: Production data is sometimes copied into the test environment
Planned control: Prohibit production data in test; use anonymised test data

Threat: Service outage lasting longer than customers accept
Vulnerability: Single-region setup; failover never tested
Planned control: Define recovery targets; test failover plan or formally accept the risk with a documented reason

Threat: Weak or reused passwords
Vulnerability: No password manager; passwords still used alongside MFA
Existing controls: Minimum password length set in Entra ID
Planned control: Roll out a company password manager; move staff towards passkeys

Threat: Sensitive data shared with the wrong people
Vulnerability: External sharing is unrestricted; no data labels
Planned control: Restrict external sharing to approved domains; introduce sensitivity labels for customer data

Threat: Security incidents not reported or reported late
Vulnerability: No known reporting channel; staff unsure what counts as an incident
Planned control: Set up an incident reporting channel and include it in onboarding and annual training

Threat: Data intercepted on home or public networks
Vulnerability: No remote working rules; no VPN or conditional access
Planned control: Publish remote working rules; enforce device firewall and conditional access for company data

Threat: Screens or devices seen or used by others at home
Vulnerability: No guidance on locking screens or shared home devices
Planned control: No new control now; include screen-lock guidance in training and review each quarter

Threat: Data subject requests handled late or wrongly
Vulnerability: No documented process or tracking for access and deletion requests
Existing controls: Requests handled by email without a process
Planned control: Document request process with 30-day tracking and a named owner

Threat: Personal data breach not reported to the authority within 72 hours
Vulnerability: No incident response plan or decision process
Planned control: Create incident response policy with severity levels, a 72-hour breach decision checklist and contact details

Threat: Incident reporting duties missed
Vulnerability: Havelmetrics has not assessed whether NIS2 applies to it as a supplier
Planned control: Complete NIS2 applicability assessment; align incident procedure with early warning (24 hours) and notification (72 hours) timelines

Threat: Inconsistent or inaccurate answers to customers
Vulnerability: Answers are written ad hoc by different people
Planned control: Maintain one approved answer library reviewed by the ISMS Manager

Threat: Customer data exposed through support tickets
Vulnerability: Broad staff access; sensitive data kept in tickets without retention limits
Existing controls: Login required for the support tool
Planned control: Role-based access; retention limits; mask sensitive data in tickets

Threat: Payment-related keys or data compromised
Vulnerability: Integration keys stored in configuration files
Existing controls: Provider handles card data on its own platform (assumed)
Planned control: Store keys in Azure Key Vault and rotate them regularly

Threat: Unauthorised physical access
Vulnerability: No visitor sign-in; keys not tracked
Planned control: Add a visitor sign-in sheet and key list; review each quarter

Threat: Known vulnerabilities in third-party libraries
Vulnerability: No automated dependency scanning or update deadline
Planned control: Enable dependency scanning (for example Dependabot); define update deadlines by severity

Threat: Ransomware encrypts systems and backups
Vulnerability: Backups not isolated; endpoint protection not centrally monitored
Planned control: Isolated or immutable backups; centrally monitored endpoint protection; least-privilege access
